title: Ana's Chia Vanilla Pudding
description: A creamy, no-cook pudding that finally puts chia seeds to good use. Sweetened with honey and scented with vanilla — the redemption arc after the ANZAC disaster.

ingredients.notes: 2 tbsp, finely ground in coffee grinder
add more if you like it sweeter.

method.instruction: Combine milk, honey, and vanilla extract in a microwave-safe bowl or jar.
Microwave on high for 50 seconds (1350W) or until warm but not boiling.
Stir well to dissolve the honey completely.
Cover and allow to cool on the counter for 5-10 minutes, stirring once or twice to prevent a skin from forming.
Add chia seeds and stir immediately to combine.
Wait 5 minutes, then stir again vigorously to break up any clumps.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Stir before serving. Top with fruit, coconut, or nuts if desired.

notes.title: Watch the Microwave
notes.content: At 1350W, 50 seconds gives warm milk. For lower wattage, increase time. For higher, decrease. Warm is perfect — hot can create a skin.

notes.title: Don't Skip the Second Stir
notes.content: Stirring at 5 minutes prevents clumps and ensures every seed hydrates evenly.

notes.title: Coconut Chia Pudding
notes.content: Replace half the milk with coconut milk and add 1 tbsp desiccated coconut.

notes.title: Chocolate Chia Pudding
notes.content: Add 1 tbsp cocoa powder and an extra 1 tbsp honey.

notes.title: Storage
notes.content: Keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days in a sealed container.
